newsitem.title: USA: Celeron seen high bidder on Elk Hills crude.
newsitem.headline: Celeron seen high bidder on Elk Hills crude.

text.p: Celeron Trading and Transportation on Tuesday was the highest bidder in the U.S. government's offering of 15,300 barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil from Elk Hills Naval Petroleum Reserve here, traders said.

The company bid $2.186 under a fixed price of $21.07 a barrel, a price based on a West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude index. Celeron bid for 7,500 bpd. Bids were for a two-month delivery period starting August 1.

Other bidders, in descending order, were as follows: Koch requested 2,010 bpd at $2.419 under the WTI price formula, EOTT Energy Partners LP wanted 2,032 bpd at a $2.471 discount to the formula price.
Two small refiners, under a special law, received the next batches of oil. Paramount was given 3,500 barrels at $2.83 a barrel under, and U.S. Oil was awarded 2,000 bpd at a $3.686 discount.
